en: I salute again and again the true Guru, Saccidānanda, the absolute embodiment of compassion, the Lord of the Yoga of Knowledge, Jñānadeva. || 1 ||
I salute again and again Jñānadeva, the Supreme Lord who transcends the states of speech, mind, and intellect, who is both partless and possessed of attributes. || 2 ||
I salute again and again Jñānadeva, who is stainless, compassionate, and peaceful; who has bowed down all limbs [of his devotees] and whose sole form is knowledge.
I bow again and again to Jñānadeva, the root of the wish-fulfilling tree of devotion, the seed of the perfection of spiritual practice, and the benefactor of all the world. (4)
Hari has manifested in person on the purifying bank of the Gautamī;
I bow again and again to that Jñānadeva, who possesses such a form. || 5 ||
I bow again and again to that Jñānadeva, by whose grace liberation has been made easily attainable for those on the path of cessation, as if by means of a staircase.
I bow again and again to Jñānadeva, who is devoted to non-duality, whose knowledge is the essence of devotion, and whose devotion is radiant with wisdom.
I bow again and again to that Jñānadeva, whose compassionate gaze always rains down nectar and whose feet are the refuge for those who prostrate. || 8 ||
I bow again and again to that Jñānadeva, whose speech is nectar-like, victorious, the quencher of suffering, and the purifier of the world. || 9 ||
I bow again and again to that Jñānadeva, the sun of the intellect, whose *Bhāvārthadīpikā* is sustained by the nectar of spiritual experience. || 10 ||
I bow again and again to Jñānadeva, whose limbs are as beautiful as the autumn moon, whose eyes are as long as lotuses, and who sits in the lotus posture. 11.
I salute again and again Jñānadeva, who is serene, supremely noble, the granter of boons, whose face bears a beautiful smile, and who is beloved by Ālānī. 12.
I bow again and again to Jñānadeva, the friend of all beings, the mother, the father, the sovereign lord, full of love and affection. 13.
I repeatedly salute Jñānadeva, who is like the autumn season for the river of the intellect, the rein for the horse of the mind, and the remover of the heat of sin. 14.
"O dear one! You yourself have said that the mother herself is beneficial to her child:
'May there always be composure of my mental fluctuations and stability of my intellect. (15)
